title: Article 75 — Other provisions as to Ministers

content.overview: Article 75 provides that the Prime Minister is appointed by the President and other Ministers are appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister; Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President; the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the House of the People; a Minister who for any period of six consecutive months is not a member of either House of Parliament ceases to be a Minister at the expiration of that period; and salaries and allowances of Ministers are as determined by Parliament by law.
content.glance: PM appointed by President; other Ministers on PM’s advice. Pleasure of President. Collective responsibility to Lok Sabha. 6-month membership rule. Salaries by law.
content.study:
Article 75 key clauses:
(1) Prime Minister appointed by the President; other Ministers appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
(2) Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President.
(3) Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the House of the People.
(4) Before a Minister enters upon office, the President administers the oaths of office and of secrecy (Third Schedule forms).
(5) A Minister who for any period of six consecutive months is not a member of either House of Parliament shall at the expiration of that period cease to be a Minister.
(6) Salaries and allowances of Ministers as determined by Parliament by law.

Collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha is the hallmark of the parliamentary system.

Examination: appointment chain; pleasure doctrine; collective responsibility to LS; 6-month non-member rule; oaths; salaries.

sections.heading: Appointment and responsibility
sections.body:
1. PM: appointed by President.
2. Other Ministers: appointed by President on advice of PM.
3. Hold office during pleasure of President.
4. Collective responsibility to the House of the People.
5. Six consecutive months without membership of either House → ceases to be Minister.
6. Salaries/allowances: Parliament by law.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain the main provisions of Article 75.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 75, the Prime Minister is appointed by the President and other Ministers are appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister. Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the House of the People. A Minister who is not a member of either House for six consecutive months ceases to be a Minister. Salaries and allowances are determined by Parliament by law.
